entries.title: I Corinthians 15:1
segments: Next, Brothers, I would remind you of the Good News which I told you, and which you received-the Good News on which you have taken your stand,

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:2
segments: And by means of which you are being saved. I would remind you of the very words that I used in telling it to you, since you are still holding fast to it, and since it was not in vain that you became believers in Christ.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:3
segments: For at the very beginning of my teaching I gave you the account which I had myself received-that Christ died for our sins (as the Scriptures had foretold),

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:4
segments: That he was buried, that on the third day he was raised (as the Scriptures had foretold),

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:5
segments: And that he appeared to Kephas, and then to the Twelve.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:6
segments: After that, he appeared to more than five hundred of our Brothers at one time, most of whom are still alive, though some have gone to their rest.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:7
segments: After that, he appeared to James, and then to all the Apostles.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:8
segments: Last of all, he appeared even to me, who am, as it were, the abortion.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:9
segments: For I am the meanest of the Apostles, I who am unworthy of the name of 'Apostle,' because I persecuted the Church of God.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:10
segments: But it is through the love of God that I am what I am, and the love that he showed me has not been wasted. No, I have toiled harder than any of them, and yet it was not I, but the love of God working with me.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:11
segments: Whether, then, it was I or whether it was they, this we proclaim, and this you believed.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:12
segments: Now, if it is proclaimed of Christ that he has been raised from the dead, how is it that some of you say that there is no such thing as a resurrection of the dead?

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:13
segments: But, if there is no such thing as a resurrection of the dead, then even Christ has not been raised;

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:14
segments: And, if Christ has not been raised, then our proclamation is without meaning, and our faith without meaning also!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:15
segments: Yes, and we are being proved to have borne false testimony about God; for we testified of God that he raised the Christ, whom he did not raise, if, indeed, the dead do not rise!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:16
segments: For, if the dead do not rise, then even Christ himself has not been raised,

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:17
segments: And, if Christ has not been raised, your faith is folly-your sins are on you still!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:18
segments: Yes, and they, who have passed to their rest in union with Christ, perished!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:19
segments: If all that we have done has been to place our hope in Christ for this life, then we of all men are the most to be pitied.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:20
segments: But, in truth, Christ has been raised from the dead, the first-fruits of those who are at rest.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:21
segments: For, since through a man there is death, so, too, through a man there is a resurrection of the dead.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:22
segments: For, as through union with Adam all men die, so through union with the Christ will all be made to live.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:23
segments: But each in his proper order-Christ the first-fruits; afterwards, at his Coming, those who belong to the Christ.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:24
segments: Then will come the end-when he surrenders the Kingdom to his God and Father, having overthrown all other rule and all other authority and power.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:25
segments: For he must reign until God 'has put all his enemies under his feet.'

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:26
segments: The last enemy to be overthrown is death;

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:27
segments: For God has placed all things under Christ's feet. (But, when it is said that all things have been placed under Christ, it is plain that God is excepted who placed everything under him.)

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:28
segments: And, when everything has been placed under him, the Son will place himself under God who placed everything under him, that God may be all in all!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:29
segments: Again, what good will they be doing who are baptized on behalf of the dead? If it is true that the dead do not rise, why are people baptized on their behalf?

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:30
segments: Why, too, do we risk our lives every hour?

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:31
segments: Daily I face death-I swear it, Brothers, by the pride in you that I feel through my union with Christ Jesus, our Lord.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:32
segments: If with only human hopes I had fought in the arena at Ephesus, what should I have gained by it? If the dead do not rise, then-'Let us eat and drink, for to-morrow we shall die'!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:33
segments: Do not be deceived. 'Good character is marred by evil company.'

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:34
segments: Awake to a righteous life, and cease to sin. There are some who have no true knowledge of God. I speak in this way to shame you.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:35
segments: Some one, however, may ask 'How do the dead rise? and in what body will they come?'

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:36
segments: You foolish man! The seed you yourself sow does not come to life, unless it dies!

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:37
segments: And when you sow, you sow not the body that will be, but a mere grain-perhaps of wheat, or something else.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:38
segments: God gives it the body that he pleases-to each seed its special body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:39
segments: All forms of life are not the same; there is one for men, another for beasts, another for birds, and another for fishes.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:40
segments: There are heavenly bodies, and earthly bodies; but the beauty of the heavenly bodies is not the beauty of the earthly.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:41
segments: There is a beauty of the sun, and a beauty of the moon, and a beauty of the stars; for even star differs from star in beauty.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:42
segments: It is the same with the resurrection of the dead. Sown a mortal body, it rises immortal; sown disfigured, it rises beautiful;

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:43
segments: Sown weak, it rises strong; sown a human body, it rises a spiritual body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:44
segments: As surely as there is a human body, there is also a spiritual body.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:45
segments: That is what is meant by the words-'Adam, the first man, became a human being'; the last Adam became a Life-giving spirit.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:46
segments: That which comes first is not the spiritual, but the human; afterwards comes the spiritual;

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:47
segments: The first man was from the dust of the earth; the second man from Heaven.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:48
segments: Those who are of the dust are like him who came from the dust; and those who are of Heaven are like him who came from Heaven.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:49
segments: And as we have borne the likeness of him who came from the dust, so let us bear the likeness of him who came from Heaven.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:50
segments: This I say, Brothers-Flesh and blood can have no share in the Kingdom of God, nor can the perishable share the imperishable.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:51
segments: Listen, I will tell you God's hidden purpose! We shall not all have passed to our rest, but we shall all be transformed-in a moment, in the twinkling of an eye,

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:52
segments: At the last trumpet-call; for the trumpet will sound, and the dead will rise immortal, and we, also, shall be transformed.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:53
segments: For this perishable body of ours must put on an imperishable form, and this dying body a deathless form.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:54
segments: And, when this dying body has put on its deathless form, then indeed will the words of Scripture come true-

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:55
segments: 'Death has been swallowed up in victory! Where, O Death, is thy victory? Where, O Death, is thy sting?'

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:56
segments: It is sin that gives death its sting, and it is the Law that gives sin its power.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:57
segments: But thanks be to God, who gives us the victory, through Jesus Christ, our Lord.

entries.title: I Corinthians 15:58
segments: Therefore, my dear Brothers, stand firm, unshaken, always diligent in the Lord's work, for you know that, in union with him, your toil is not in vain.
